def write_pyramid_task(
    pyramid: Mapping[int, xr.Dataset],
    task: WriteTask,
    s3_options: S3Options | None = None,
) -> WriteTask:
    """Write one task's region of *pyramid* into an initialised store.

    This is the function an array-job element calls.  It is safe to run
    any number of tasks of the same manifest concurrently, on any number
    of nodes, without locks: the planner guarantees that no two tasks
    share a zarr chunk (or shard).  Re-running a task overwrites the
    same region with the same data, so retries are harmless.

    Parameters
    ----------
    pyramid:
        Mapping of level to dataset, built the same way as for the init
        step (same levels, variables, dimension lengths).  It may cover
        either the **full** extent of the split dimensions, in which case
        the task region is selected here, or **only the task region**,
        e.g. because the source was subset with
        ``source.isel(task.isel())`` before regridding.  The second form
        is usually much cheaper, since only the task's slice of the
        source is read and regridded.  Datasets may contain more
        variables or levels than the task needs; they are ignored.
    task:
        The work unit, as taken from ``manifest.tasks``.
    s3_options:
        Options for :class:`s3fs.S3FileSystem`.  Credentials are never
        stored in the manifest, so every worker passes its own.

    Returns
    -------
    WriteTask
        *task* itself, after the data and the completion marker have
        been written.  Returning the task (rather than nothing) makes
        the result usable as a cache key: reflow can check a cached
        result with ``verify=is_task_done``.

    Raises
    ------
    StaleTaskError
        The store was re-initialised after *task* was planned.
    ManifestError
        *task* is not identical to the task of the same id in the stored
        manifest (only tasks the manifest validated are written), or
        *pyramid* does not match the manifest (missing level or variable,
        different dimension lengths, a region the data cannot cover), or
        its coordinate values in the task region differ from the ones the
        init stored (e.g. another time range of the same length).
    """
    started = time.monotonic()
    target = _Target(task.path, s3_options)
    manifest = load_manifest(task.path, s3_options)
    if manifest.manifest_id != task.manifest_id:
        raise StaleTaskError(
            f"{task.task_id} belongs to manifest {task.manifest_id}, but "
            f"{task.path} was re-initialised with manifest "
            f"{manifest.manifest_id}; plan the tasks again from the new manifest"
        )
    try:
        planned = manifest.task(task.task_id)
    except KeyError:
        raise ManifestError(f"{task.task_id} is not part of manifest {manifest.manifest_id}") from None
    if planned != task:
        # The manifest validated that its own tasks are chunk-aligned and
        # disjoint; a task that differs (edited or hand-built) has no such
        # guarantee and could race with another worker.
        raise ManifestError(
            f"{task.task_id} differs from the task stored in the manifest "
            f"({task} != {planned}); use the tasks of the stored manifest"
        )

    writes: list[DeferredWrite] = []
    for level in task.levels:
        if level not in pyramid:
            raise ManifestError(
                f"{task.task_id} writes level {level}, but the pyramid only has levels {sorted(pyramid)}"
            )
        spec = manifest.level(level)
        store = target.store(spec.store)
        group = zarr.open_group(store, mode="r+", zarr_format=task.zarr_format)
        encodings = stored_encodings(store, zarr_format=task.zarr_format)
        for name in task.variables:
            array_spec = spec.array(name)
            if name not in pyramid[level]:
                raise ManifestError(f"{task.task_id}: variable {name!r} missing on level {level}")
            var = _select_region(pyramid[level][name].variable, array_spec, task)
            var = var.copy(deep=False)
            var.encoding = encodings.get(name, {})
            encoded = encode_zarr_variable(var, name=name, zarr_format=task.zarr_format)
            offsets = _region_offsets(array_spec, task)
            source = _aligned(encoded.data, array_spec.chunks, offsets, name)
            region = tuple(slice(off, off + n) for off, n in zip(offsets, encoded.shape))
            writes.append(DeferredWrite(source, get_array(group, name), region))

        mismatches = coordinate_differences(
            pyramid[level],
            store,
            spec.coords,
            zarr_format=task.zarr_format,
            region={dim: (start, stop) for dim, start, stop in task.region},
        )
        if mismatches:
            raise ManifestError(
                f"{task.task_id}: the pyramid does not match the coordinates "
                f"stored by the init on level {level} ("
                + "; ".join(mismatches)
                + ").  It was built from other data than the store; nothing "
                "was written."
            )

    store_all(writes)
    # The manifest was checked before writing.  If the store was
    # re-initialised meanwhile (an overwrite while this task ran), the
    # data above may have landed in the new stores: fail loudly instead
    # of reporting success, and never write a marker for it.
    if not is_current(task, s3_options):
        raise StaleTaskError(
            f"{task.path} was re-initialised while {task.task_id} was writing; "
            "its data may have been written into the new stores.  Do not "
            "re-initialise a store while a conversion into it is running."
        )
    marker = {
        "manifest_id": task.manifest_id,
        "task_id": task.task_id,
        "finished": datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
        "elapsed_s": round(time.monotonic() - started, 3),
        "host": socket.gethostname(),
        "variables": list(task.variables),
        "levels": list(task.levels),
        "region": {d: [a, b] for d, a, b in task.region},
    }
    target.write_text(json.dumps(marker, indent=2), STATE_DIR, DONE_DIR, f"{task.task_id}.json")
    logger.info(
        "%s done (%s, %d level(s)) in %.1fs",
        task.task_id,
        ", ".join(task.variables),
        len(task.levels),
        marker["elapsed_s"],
    )
    return task

The check is cheap: it reads the level metadata and lists one small marker file per finished task. It does not read any data.

A store is complete when

  1. the stored manifest is the one being checked (the store was not re-initialised in between),
  2. every level store and every array exists with the shape, write unit and dtype recorded in the manifest, and
  3. every task has written its completion marker.

def check_pyramid_store(
    manifest: PyramidManifest | str,
    s3_options: S3Options | None = None,
    *,
    inspect_chunks: bool = False,
) -> StoreReport:
    """Check whether a store is complete according to its manifest.

    The check is cheap: it reads the level metadata and lists one small
    marker file per finished task.  It does **not** read any data.

    A store is complete when

    1. the stored manifest is the one being checked (the store was not
       re-initialised in between),
    2. every level store and every array exists with the shape, write
       unit and dtype recorded in the manifest, and
    3. every task has written its completion marker.

    Parameters
    ----------
    manifest:
        The manifest returned by
        [`init_pyramid_store`][grid_doctor.init_pyramid_store],
        or the pyramid root path, in which case the stored manifest is
        loaded.
    s3_options:
        Options for :class:`s3fs.S3FileSystem` (S3 targets only).
    inspect_chunks:
        Also list the stored chunk keys and report, per finished task,
        how many chunks of its region are absent.  This lists every
        object of every array and can be slow on large S3 stores.  It
        never makes a store incomplete; see
        [`StoreReport.absent_chunks`][grid_doctor.StoreReport].

    Returns
    -------
    StoreReport
        Use ``report.complete`` (or ``bool(report)``),
        ``report.missing_tasks`` and ``report.summary()``; call
        ``report.raise_if_incomplete()`` to fail a workflow step.
    """
    if isinstance(manifest, str):
        manifest = load_manifest(manifest, s3_options)
    target = _Target(manifest.path, s3_options)
    problems: list[str] = []

    stored_text = target.read_text(STATE_DIR, MANIFEST_FILE)
    if stored_text is None:
        interrupted = _interrupted_init(target)
        problems.append(
            f"no manifest stored at {manifest.path}/{STATE_DIR}" + (f": {interrupted}" if interrupted else "")
        )
    else:
        stored_id = json.loads(stored_text).get("manifest_id")
        if stored_id != manifest.manifest_id:
            problems.append(f"store was re-initialised: it holds manifest {stored_id}, not {manifest.manifest_id}")

    groups: dict[int, zarr.Group] = {}
    for spec in manifest.levels:
        try:
            group = zarr.open_group(target.store(spec.store), mode="r", zarr_format=manifest.zarr_format)
        except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - report, do not raise
            problems.append(f"level {spec.level}: cannot open {spec.store}: {error}")
            continue
        groups[spec.level] = group
        members = set(group.array_keys())
        for name in spec.coords:
            if name not in members:
                problems.append(f"level {spec.level}: coordinate {name!r} missing")
        for array_spec in spec.data_vars:
            problems.extend(_check_array(spec.level, group, members, array_spec))

    known = {t.task_id for t in manifest.tasks}
    done: set[str] = set()
    stale = 0
    for filename in target.list_dir(STATE_DIR, DONE_DIR):
        if not filename.endswith(".json") or filename.startswith("."):
            continue
        text = target.read_text(STATE_DIR, DONE_DIR, filename)
        try:
            marker = json.loads(text or "")
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            stale += 1
            continue
        task_id = marker.get("task_id")
        if marker.get("manifest_id") == manifest.manifest_id and task_id in known:
            done.add(str(task_id))
        else:
            stale += 1

    order = [t.task_id for t in manifest.tasks]
    done_tasks = tuple(t for t in order if t in done)
    missing = tuple(t for t in order if t not in done)

    absent: list[tuple[str, int, int]] = []
    if inspect_chunks:
        absent = _absent_chunks(manifest, target, groups, [manifest.task(t) for t in done_tasks])

    return StoreReport(
        manifest_id=manifest.manifest_id,
        n_tasks=len(manifest.tasks),
        done_tasks=done_tasks,
        missing_tasks=missing,
        problems=tuple(problems),
        stale_markers=stale,
        absent_chunks=tuple(absent),
    )

def select_tasks(self, task_ids: Iterable[str]) -> list[WriteTask]:
    """Return the tasks with the given ids, in manifest order.

    Handy for re-submitting only what
    [`check_pyramid_store`][grid_doctor.check_pyramid_store] reported
    as missing::

        retry = manifest.select_tasks(report.missing_tasks)
    """
    wanted = set(task_ids)
    unknown = wanted - {t.task_id for t in self.tasks}
    if unknown:
        raise KeyError(f"unknown task ids: {sorted(unknown)}")
    return [t for t in self.tasks if t.task_id in wanted]

def summary(self) -> str:
    """One human-readable paragraph."""
    state = "complete" if self.complete else "INCOMPLETE"
    lines = [(f"Store {state}: {len(self.done_tasks)}/{self.n_tasks} task(s) done (manifest {self.manifest_id}).")]
    if self.missing_tasks:
        shown = ", ".join(self.missing_tasks[:10])
        more = len(self.missing_tasks) - 10
        lines.append(f"Missing: {shown}" + (f" and {more} more." if more > 0 else "."))
    lines.extend(f"Problem: {p}" for p in self.problems)
    if self.stale_markers:
        lines.append(f"Ignored {self.stale_markers} stale marker(s).")
    if self.absent_chunks:
        absent = sum(a for _, a, _ in self.absent_chunks)
        lines.append(
            f"{absent} chunk(s) not stored in {len(self.absent_chunks)} finished "
            "task(s) (all-fill-value chunks are skipped by zarr; this is "
            "expected for masked or regional data)."

    return "\n".join(lines)

def is_current(item: PyramidManifest | WriteTask, s3_options: S3Options | None = None) -> bool:
    """Whether the store at ``item.path`` still holds ``item``'s manifest.

    ``False`` if the store was deleted, never finished its init, or was
    re-initialised since *item* was created.  Meant as a cache check, for
    example reflow's ``verify=`` hook on the init step: a cached manifest
    is only reusable while the store it describes still exists.

    Parameters
    ----------
    item:
        A manifest or any of its tasks.
    s3_options:
        Options for :class:`s3fs.S3FileSystem` (S3 targets only).
    """
    text = _Target(item.path, s3_options).read_text(STATE_DIR, MANIFEST_FILE)
    if text is None:
        return False
    try:
        stored_id = json.loads(text).get("manifest_id")
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        return False
    return bool(stored_id == item.manifest_id)

    """Whether *task* has a completion marker for the current manifest.

    Equivalent to ``task.task_id in check_pyramid_store(...).done_tasks``
    but reads a single small file, so it is cheap enough to call per
    task, e.g. as reflow's ``verify=`` hook on the array job.

    Parameters
    ----------
    task:
        The work unit.
    s3_options:
        Options for :class:`s3fs.S3FileSystem` (S3 targets only).

    if not is_current(task, s3_options):
        return False
    text = _Target(task.path, s3_options).read_text(STATE_DIR, DONE_DIR, f"{task.task_id}.json")
    if text is None:
        return False
    try:
        marker = json.loads(text)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        return False
    return bool(marker.get("manifest_id") == task.manifest_id and marker.get("task_id") == task.task_id)

Create a multi-resolution HEALPix pyramid.

The input dataset is first remapped to max_level with regrid_to_healpix. For nested output ordering, lower levels are derived efficiently with coarsen_healpix. For ring ordering, each lower level is regenerated directly from the source dataset.

For dask-backed input the result is lazy and chunked along cell (cell_chunks, forwarded to regrid_to_healpix); coarser levels keep that chunk size. Every level builds on the finest one, so write the pyramid with save_pyramid, which computes all levels in one pass. Calling .compute() per level instead regrids the source once per level.

def create_healpix_pyramid(
    ds: xr.Dataset,
    max_level: int | None = None,
    min_level: int = 0,
    *,
    coarsen_mode: CoarsenMode = "auto",
    min_valid_fraction: float = 0.5,
    valid_fraction: ValidFraction = False,
    **kwargs: Unpack[RegridOptions],
) -> dict[int, xr.Dataset]:
    """Create a multi-resolution HEALPix pyramid.

    The input dataset is first remapped to *max_level* with
    [`regrid_to_healpix`][grid_doctor.remap.regrid_to_healpix].
    For nested output ordering, lower levels are derived efficiently
    with
    [`coarsen_healpix`][grid_doctor.coarsen_healpix].
    For ring ordering, each lower level is regenerated directly from
    the source dataset.

    For dask-backed input the result is lazy and chunked along ``cell``
    (``cell_chunks``, forwarded to
    [`regrid_to_healpix`][grid_doctor.remap.regrid_to_healpix]); coarser
    levels keep that chunk size.  Every level builds on the finest one,
    so write the pyramid with
    [`save_pyramid`][grid_doctor.save_pyramid], which computes
    all levels in one pass.  Calling ``.compute()`` per level instead
    regrids the source once per level.

    Parameters
    ----------
    ds:
        Source dataset.
    max_level:
        Finest HEALPix level.
    min_level:
        Coarsest HEALPix level to keep.
    coarsen_mode:
        Coarsening strategy for building lower pyramid levels.
        ``"mean"`` for continuous data, ``"mode"`` for categorical,
        ``"auto"`` to infer from the remapping method.
    min_valid_fraction:
        Minimum fraction of valid children for a parent cell to be
        valid.  Default ``0.5``.
    valid_fraction:
        Store ``<name>_valid_fraction`` next to the selected variables on
        every level: the fraction of valid finest-level cells under each
        cell, as float32, linked via the CF ``ancillary_variables``
        attribute.  Cell values are means over their valid area, so
        global or regional means over a coarse level need these weights,
        e.g. ``ds.sst.weighted(ds.sst_valid_fraction.fillna(0)).mean("cell")``.

        ``False`` (default) stores nothing.  ``True`` gives every cell
        variable a fraction of its full shape (correct for masks that
        change over time or height).  ``"static"`` stores one ``cell``-only
        fraction from the first slice along all other dimensions -- small,
        but only correct when the mask never changes (e.g. land/sea).
        A list of names selects variables (full shape); a mapping such as
        ``{"sst": "static", "ice": True}`` sets the shape per variable.
        Requires nested ordering.
    **kwargs:
        Forwarded to
        [`regrid_to_healpix`][grid_doctor.remap.regrid_to_healpix].

    Returns
    -------
    dict[int, xarray.Dataset]
        Pyramid keyed by level.
    """
    if max_level is None:
        max_level = resolution_to_healpix_level(get_latlon_resolution(ds))

    is_nested = bool(kwargs.get("nest", True))
    if not is_nested and valid_fraction is not False:
        raise ValueError("valid_fraction requires nested ordering (nest=True).")

    pyramid: dict[int, xr.Dataset] = {}
    finest = regrid_to_healpix(ds, max_level, **kwargs)
    pyramid[max_level] = finest

    if is_nested:
        fractions = resolve_valid_fraction(valid_fraction, finest)
        pyramid[max_level] = with_finest_fractions(finest, fractions, max_level)
        pyramid.update(
            coarse_levels(
                finest,
                max_level=max_level,
                min_level=min_level,
                coarsen_mode=resolve_coarsen_mode(finest, coarsen_mode),
                min_valid_fraction=min_valid_fraction,
                mode_kernel=_coarsen_array_mode,
                valid_fraction=fractions,
            )
        )
        return pyramid

    for level in range(max_level - 1, min_level - 1, -1):
        pyramid[level] = regrid_to_healpix(ds, level, **kwargs)
    return pyramid

items.text:
Coarsen a HEALPix dataset to a lower-resolution level.

The coarsening is performed as a single reshape + reduction over all batch dimensions simultaneously, without per-slice Python loops.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default ds Dataset

HEALPix dataset with a cell dimension and grid-doctor metadata (see grid_doctor.metadata).

required target_level int

Target HEALPix level (must be lower than the current level).

required coarsen_mode CoarsenMode

"mean": NaN-aware averaging for continuous fields. "mode": most frequent value for categorical fields. "auto": infer from the production method recorded for the dataset: "nearest" and "binned-mode" give mode, everything else mean. The mode is chosen once for the whole dataset; coarsen continuous and categorical variables in separate calls when a dataset mixes both, for example after binning with agg={"radiance": "mean", "cloud_type": "mode"}.

'auto' min_valid_fraction float

Minimum fraction of valid (non-NaN) children required to produce a valid parent cell. Parents with fewer valid children are set to NaN. Default 0.5 (at least half of the children must be valid).

0.5 valid_fraction ValidFraction

Add <name>_valid_fraction variables: the fraction of valid cells of ds under each coarse cell (see create_healpix_pyramid). Fractions are relative to the level of ds, so coarsen from the finest level to get weights for exact global means.

False

Returns:

Type Description Dataset

Coarsened dataset.

Notes

Nested HEALPix indices have a direct parent-child relationship: pixel i at level L contains children 4*i to 4*i+3 at level L+1. Coarsening therefore reduces to grouping contiguous blocks of 4**delta_level child cells and averaging (or taking the mode for categorical data).

Ring-ordered datasets do not have contiguous parent-child layout and must be remapped directly at each target level.

With coarsen_mode="mean", always coarsen from the finest level rather than chaining level by level. A chained mean weights every valid parent equally, regardless of how many valid finest-level cells it was built from, so data with NaNs (land, sea ice, observation gaps) drifts between levels.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

When the ordering is not nested, or target_level is not lower than the current level.

def coarsen_healpix(
    ds: xr.Dataset,
    target_level: int,
    coarsen_mode: CoarsenMode = "auto",
    min_valid_fraction: float = 0.5,
    valid_fraction: ValidFraction = False,
) -> xr.Dataset:
    """Coarsen a HEALPix dataset to a lower-resolution level.

    The coarsening is performed as a single reshape + reduction over
    all batch dimensions simultaneously, without per-slice Python loops.

    Parameters
    ----------
    ds:
        HEALPix dataset with a ``cell`` dimension and grid-doctor
        metadata (see [`grid_doctor.metadata`][grid_doctor.metadata]).
    target_level:
        Target HEALPix level (must be lower than the current level).
    coarsen_mode:
        ``"mean"``: NaN-aware averaging for continuous fields.
        ``"mode"``: most frequent value for categorical fields.
        ``"auto"``: infer from the production method recorded for the
        dataset: ``"nearest"`` and ``"binned-mode"`` give mode,
        everything else mean.  The mode is chosen once for the whole
        dataset; coarsen continuous and categorical variables in
        separate calls when a dataset mixes both, for example after
        binning with ``agg={"radiance": "mean", "cloud_type": "mode"}``.
    min_valid_fraction:
        Minimum fraction of valid (non-NaN) children required to
        produce a valid parent cell.  Parents with fewer valid
        children are set to NaN.  Default ``0.5`` (at least half
        of the children must be valid).
    valid_fraction:
        Add ``<name>_valid_fraction`` variables: the fraction of valid
        cells of *ds* under each coarse cell (see
        [`create_healpix_pyramid`][grid_doctor.create_healpix_pyramid]).
        Fractions are relative to the level of *ds*, so coarsen from the
        finest level to get weights for exact global means.

    Returns
    -------
    xarray.Dataset
        Coarsened dataset.

    Notes
    -----
    Nested HEALPix indices have a direct parent-child relationship:
    pixel *i* at level *L* contains children ``4*i`` to ``4*i+3`` at
    level *L+1*.  Coarsening therefore reduces to grouping contiguous
    blocks of ``4**delta_level`` child cells and averaging (or taking
    the mode for categorical data).

    Ring-ordered datasets do not have contiguous parent-child layout
    and must be remapped directly at each target level.

    With ``coarsen_mode="mean"``, always coarsen from the finest level
    rather than chaining level by level.  A chained mean weights every
    valid parent equally, regardless of how many valid finest-level
    cells it was built from, so data with NaNs (land, sea ice,
    observation gaps) drifts between levels.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        When the ordering is not nested, or *target_level* is not
        lower than the current level.
    """
    grid = HealpixMetadata.from_dataset(ds).grid
    if not grid.nest:
        raise ValueError(
            "coarsen_healpix only supports nested HEALPix ordering. "
            "Use create_healpix_pyramid(..., nest=False) to "
            "regenerate ring levels directly."
        )
    current_level = grid.level
    if target_level >= current_level:
        raise ValueError("target_level must be lower than the current HEALPix level.")

    return coarsen_dataset(
        ds,
        source_level=current_level,
        target_level=target_level,
        coarsen_mode=resolve_coarsen_mode(ds, coarsen_mode),
        min_valid_fraction=min_valid_fraction,
        mode_kernel=_coarsen_array_mode,
        valid_fraction=valid_fraction,
    )

def get_latlon_resolution(ds: xr.Dataset) -> float:
    """Estimate the horizontal resolution of *ds* in degrees.

    Parameters
    ----------
    ds:
        Dataset on a regular lon/lat grid, a curvilinear grid, or an
        unstructured grid.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        Approximate grid spacing in degrees.

    Examples
    --------
    ```python
    resolution = get_latlon_resolution(ds)
    level = resolution_to_healpix_level(resolution)
    ```
    """
    if _is_unstructured(ds):
        cell_dim = _get_unstructured_dim(ds)
        n_cells = ds.sizes[cell_dim]
        return float(np.degrees(np.sqrt(4.0 * np.pi / float(n_cells))))

    lat, lon = _get_latlon_arrays(ds)
    if lat.ndim == 1:
        lat_res = float(np.nanmin(np.abs(np.diff(lat))))
        lon_res = float(np.nanmin(np.abs(np.diff(lon))))
    else:
        lat_res = float(np.nanmean(np.abs(np.diff(lat, axis=0))))
        lon_res = float(np.nanmean(np.abs(np.diff(lon, axis=1))))
    return min(lat_res, lon_res)


    if resolution_deg <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("resolution_deg must be positive.")
    level = int(np.round(np.log2(58.6 / resolution_deg)))
    return max(0, level)

items.text:
Apply a previously generated ESMF weight file to ds.

Uses the batched engine in grid_doctor.remap._sparse which replaces per-slice vectorize=True with a single batched sparse matmul for a typical 10–50× speedup.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default ds Dataset

Source dataset to remap.

required weights_path str | Path

Path to the NetCDF weight file.

required missing_policy MissingPolicy

Strategy for handling NaN (missing) values in the source grid during weight application.

"renormalize" (default) Source cells that are NaN are excluded from the weighted sum and the weights of the remaining valid source cells are rescaled so they sum to 1. A target cell receives a valid value as long as at least one contributing source cell is valid. This is the right choice for most climate fields: for instance, a HEALPix cell on a coastline that partly overlaps land (NaN) and partly ocean still receives a valid SST from the ocean fraction.

"propagate" If any contributing source cell is NaN, the target cell is set to NaN: no partial averages. Use this when completeness of the source coverage matters more than spatial coverage of the output, for example when computing area-integrated flux budgets where a partial average would bias the integral. Note that this is very aggressive: a single NaN source cell at the edge of a target cell's footprint is enough to discard it. For conservative remapping where a HEALPix cell can overlap dozens of source cells, large portions of the output along coastlines, swath edges, and orbit gaps will be NaN.

'renormalize' grid Dataset | None

Optional grid dataset with source geometry.

None source_dims tuple[str, ...] | None

Optional explicit source dimensions.

None source_units SourceUnits

Unit convention for geometry-based inference.

'auto' backend ApplyBackend

Application backend ("auto", "scipy", "numba").

'auto' cell_chunks int | Literal['auto'] | None

Chunk size of the output along cell for dask-backed input. Each output chunk is computed from its own slice of weight-matrix rows, so no task holds the whole HEALPix field. "auto" uses DEFAULT_CELL_CHUNK cells (rounded to a multiple of 4), None produces a single chunk. NumPy-backed input is always computed in one piece.

'auto' ellipsoid Ellipsoid | None

Ellipsoid the weights must have been generated on. None (default) takes the one recorded in the weight file (a sphere for files that record none); the HEALPix cell centres are computed on it.

None nest bool | None

HEALPix order of the output: nested when True, ring when False. None (default) keeps the order of the weight file. Stored weight files are nested; their rows are renumbered for ring output, so one file serves both orders.

None

Returns:

Type Description Dataset

Dataset on the HEALPix target grid with a cell dimension.

Examples:

ds_hp = apply_weight_file(ds_icon, "icon_to_healpix_d8.nc")

def apply_weight_file(
    ds: xr.Dataset,
    weights_path: str | Path,
    *,
    missing_policy: MissingPolicy = "renormalize",
    grid: xr.Dataset | None = None,
    source_dims: tuple[str, ...] | None = None,
    source_units: SourceUnits = "auto",
    backend: ApplyBackend = "auto",
    cell_chunks: int | Literal["auto"] | None = "auto",
    ellipsoid: Ellipsoid | None = None,
    nest: bool | None = None,
) -> xr.Dataset:
    """Apply a previously generated ESMF weight file to *ds*.

    Uses the batched engine in
    `grid_doctor.remap._sparse` which replaces per-slice
    ``vectorize=True`` with a single batched sparse matmul for a
    typical 10–50× speedup.

    Parameters
    ----------
    ds:
        Source dataset to remap.
    weights_path:
        Path to the NetCDF weight file.
    missing_policy:
        Strategy for handling NaN (missing) values in the source
        grid during weight application.

        ``"renormalize"`` (default)
            Source cells that are NaN are excluded from the
            weighted sum and the weights of the remaining valid
            source cells are rescaled so they sum to 1.  A target
            cell receives a valid value as long as **at least one**
            contributing source cell is valid.  This is the right
            choice for most climate fields: for instance, a
            HEALPix cell on a coastline that partly overlaps land
            (NaN) and partly ocean still receives a valid SST from
            the ocean fraction.

        ``"propagate"``
            If **any** contributing source cell is NaN, the target
            cell is set to NaN: no partial averages.  Use this
            when completeness of the source coverage matters more
            than spatial coverage of the output, for example when
            computing area-integrated flux budgets where a partial
            average would bias the integral.  Note that this is
            very aggressive: a single NaN source cell at the edge
            of a target cell's footprint is enough to discard it.
            For conservative remapping where a HEALPix cell can
            overlap dozens of source cells, large portions of the
            output along coastlines, swath edges, and orbit gaps
            will be NaN.
    grid:
        Optional grid dataset with source geometry.
    source_dims:
        Optional explicit source dimensions.
    source_units:
        Unit convention for geometry-based inference.
    backend:
        Application backend (``"auto"``, ``"scipy"``, ``"numba"``).

    cell_chunks:
        Chunk size of the output along ``cell`` for dask-backed input.
        Each output chunk is computed from its own slice of weight-matrix
        rows, so no task holds the whole HEALPix field.  ``"auto"`` uses
        ``DEFAULT_CELL_CHUNK`` cells (rounded to a multiple of 4), ``None``
        produces a single chunk.  NumPy-backed input is always computed
        in one piece.
    ellipsoid:
        Ellipsoid the weights must have been generated on.  ``None``
        (default) takes the one recorded in the weight file (a sphere
        for files that record none); the HEALPix cell centres are
        computed on it.
    nest:
        HEALPix order of the output: nested when ``True``, ring when
        ``False``. ``None`` (default) keeps the order of the weight file.
        Stored weight files are nested; their rows are renumbered for
        ring output, so one file serves both orders.

    Returns
    -------
    xarray.Dataset
        Dataset on the HEALPix target grid with a ``cell`` dimension.

    Examples
    --------
    ```python
    ds_hp = apply_weight_file(ds_icon, "icon_to_healpix_d8.nc")
    ```
    """
    if missing_policy not in {"renormalize", "propagate"}:
        raise ValueError("missing_policy must be 'renormalize' or 'propagate'.")

    matrix, n_target, n_source, level, order, method, stored_sd, stored_ellipsoid = _read_weight_file(
        weights_path, nest=nest
    )
    # Checked before regridding, so a mismatch fails fast.
    ellipsoid = _weights_ellipsoid(ellipsoid, stored_ellipsoid, weights_path)

    resolved_sd = _resolve_source_dims_for_weight_application(
        ds,
        n_source=n_source,
        grid=grid,
        source_dims=source_dims,
        source_units=source_units,
        stored_source_dims=stored_sd,
    )
    n_src_dims = len(resolved_sd)
    cell_chunk = _resolve_cell_chunk(cell_chunks, n_target)
    row_blocks: list[csr_matrix] | None = None

    regridded: dict[str, xr.DataArray] = {}
    for name, data in ds.data_vars.items():
        if not set(resolved_sd).issubset(map(str, data.dims)):
            regridded[str(name)] = data
            continue

        if cell_chunk is not None and data.chunks is not None:
            if row_blocks is None:
                row_blocks = _row_blocks(matrix, cell_chunk)
            regridded[str(name)] = _apply_weights_rowblocked(
                data,
                resolved_sd,
                row_blocks,
                missing_policy=missing_policy,
                backend=backend,
                parallel=False,
            )
            continue

        regridded[str(name)] = cast(
            xr.DataArray,
            xr.apply_ufunc(
                apply_weights_nd,
                data,
                input_core_dims=[list(resolved_sd)],
                output_core_dims=[["cell"]],
                exclude_dims=set(resolved_sd),
                dask="parallelized",
                kwargs={
                    "matrix": matrix,
                    "n_source_dims": n_src_dims,
                    "missing_policy": missing_policy,
                    "backend": backend,
                    # dask already runs tasks in parallel threads; nested
                    # thread teams exhaust the process thread limit.
                    "parallel": data.chunks is None,
                },
                output_dtypes=[np.float64],
                dask_gufunc_kwargs={"output_sizes": {"cell": n_target}},
            ),
        )

    result = xr.Dataset(regridded, attrs=ds.attrs.copy())
    if level >= 0:
        target_grid = HealpixGrid.from_nest(
            level,
            nest=(order == "nested"),
            ellipsoid=ellipsoid,
        )
        result = _attach_healpix_coords(result, target_grid, method=method)
    return result

def select_bbox(
    ds: xr.Dataset,
    *,
    lon: tuple[float, float],
    lat: tuple[float, float],
    level: int | None = None,
    query_delta: int = _DEFAULT_QUERY_DELTA,
    load: bool = True,
) -> xr.Dataset:
    """Extract all cells covering a geographic bounding box.

    The box is rasterised at the coarse level ``level - query_delta``;
    every coarse parent expands to one contiguous fine-level range of
    ``4**query_delta`` cells.  The result therefore *covers* the box
    (cells straddling the edge are included) with read granularity set
    by *query_delta*; align it with the store's chunk exponent for
    reads with zero waste.

    Parameters
    ----------
    ds:
        HEALPix dataset (see [`select_cells`][grid_doctor.select_cells]).
    lon:
        ``(west, east)`` longitude bounds in degrees.
    lat:
        ``(south, north)`` latitude bounds in degrees.
    level:
        HEALPix level override.
    query_delta:
        Level offset for the coverage query.  Larger values mean fewer,
        larger contiguous reads; smaller values follow the box outline
        more tightly.
    load:
        Load the selection into memory (default).

    Returns
    -------
    xarray.Dataset
        Compact subset covering the box.
    """
    resolved_level = _dataset_level(ds, level)
    query_level = max(0, resolved_level - query_delta)
    query_grid = HealpixGrid(level=query_level, ellipsoid=_dataset_ellipsoid(ds))
    module, kwargs = _require_healpix_geo_module(query_grid)
    coverage = np.asarray(
        module.zone_coverage(
            (lon[0], lat[0], lon[1], lat[1]),
            query_level,
            flat=True,
            **kwargs,
        )
    )
    parents = coverage[0].astype(np.int64)
    ranges = _parents_to_ranges(parents, resolved_level - query_level)
    logger.info(
        "Bounding box resolves to %d parent cells at level %d (%d contiguous ranges at level %d).",
        parents.size,
        query_level,
        len(ranges),
        resolved_level,
    )
    cells = np.concatenate([np.arange(a, b, dtype=np.int64) for a, b in ranges])
    return select_cells(ds, cells, level=resolved_level, load=load)

def select_cone(
    ds: xr.Dataset,
    *,
    lon: float,
    lat: float,
    radius: float,
    level: int | None = None,
    query_delta: int = _DEFAULT_QUERY_DELTA,
    load: bool = True,
) -> xr.Dataset:
    """Extract all cells within *radius* degrees of a centre point.

    Parameters
    ----------
    ds:
        HEALPix dataset (see [`select_cells`][grid_doctor.select_cells]).
    lon, lat:
        Centre coordinates in degrees.
    radius:
        Angular radius in degrees.
    level:
        HEALPix level override.
    query_delta:
        Level offset for the coverage query.
    load:
        Load the selection into memory (default).

    Returns
    -------
    xarray.Dataset
        Compact subset covering the cone.
    """
    resolved_level = _dataset_level(ds, level)
    query_level = max(0, resolved_level - query_delta)
    query_grid = HealpixGrid(level=query_level, ellipsoid=_dataset_ellipsoid(ds))
    module, kwargs = _require_healpix_geo_module(query_grid)
    coverage = np.asarray(module.cone_coverage((lon, lat), radius, query_level, flat=True, **kwargs))
    parents = coverage[0].astype(np.int64)
    ranges = _parents_to_ranges(parents, resolved_level - query_level)
    cells = np.concatenate([np.arange(a, b, dtype=np.int64) for a, b in ranges])
    return select_cells(ds, cells, level=resolved_level, load=load)

def select_cells(
    ds: xr.Dataset,
    cells: Int64Array | list[int],
    *,
    level: int | None = None,
    load: bool = True,
) -> xr.Dataset:
    """Extract the given HEALPix cells from a dataset.

    Works on dense datasets (positional index equals cell ID, with or
    without materialised coordinates) and on compact subsets (``cell``
    coordinate holds actual IDs).  Contiguous ID runs are read as
    contiguous slices, so a spatially compact selection touches only
    the chunks it needs.

    Parameters
    ----------
    ds:
        HEALPix dataset, typically opened with
        ``xr.open_zarr(store, chunks=None)``.
    cells:
        Global HEALPix cell IDs to extract (any order; duplicates are
        dropped).
    level:
        HEALPix level override when the dataset has no HEALPix grid
        mapping.
    load:
        Load the selected data into memory (default).  The selection is
        small by construction; that is the point of selecting.

    Returns
    -------
    xarray.Dataset
        Compact subset: ``cell`` coordinate holds the requested IDs,
        cell-centre ``latitude``/``longitude`` are attached, and the
        subset is marked sparse.
    """
    _require_nested(ds)
    resolved_level = _dataset_level(ds, level)
    wanted = np.unique(np.asarray(cells, dtype=np.int64))
    if wanted.size == 0:
        raise ValueError("No cells requested.")
    npix = 12 * 4**resolved_level
    if int(wanted[0]) < 0 or int(wanted[-1]) >= npix:
        raise ValueError(f"Cell IDs must be within [0, {npix}) for level {resolved_level}.")

    if "cell" in ds.coords:
        # Compact dataset (or legacy dense store with coordinates):
        # positions are found through the coordinate values.
        coord = np.asarray(ds["cell"].values, dtype=np.int64)
        pos = np.searchsorted(coord, wanted)
        pos = np.clip(pos, 0, coord.size - 1)
        present = coord[pos] == wanted
        if not present.all():
            missing = wanted[~present]
            raise KeyError(
                f"{missing.size} requested cells are not present in the dataset (first missing: {int(missing[0])})."
            )
        pieces = [ds.isel(cell=slice(a, b)) for a, b in _contiguous_runs(pos)]
    else:
        # Dense store without materialised coordinates: positional
        # index *is* the cell ID.
        pieces = [ds.isel(cell=slice(a, b)) for a, b in _contiguous_runs(wanted)]

    subset = pieces[0] if len(pieces) == 1 else xr.concat(pieces, dim="cell", data_vars="minimal", coords="minimal")
    if load:
        subset = subset.load()
    return attach_cell_coords(subset, wanted, level=resolved_level, attrs=ds.attrs)

def attach_cell_coords(
    ds: xr.Dataset,
    cells: Int64Array,
    *,
    level: int,
    attrs: Mapping[Hashable, object] | None = None,
) -> xr.Dataset:
    """Attach computed cell coordinates to a compact subset.

    HEALPix coordinates are a pure function of the cell index; stores
    written with ``write_coords=False`` carry none, and this function
    reconstructs them for exactly the cells at hand, on the ellipsoid
    recorded in *ds* (the configured one if *ds* has no HEALPix metadata).

    Parameters
    ----------
    ds:
        Subset whose ``cell`` dimension corresponds to *cells*.
    cells:
        Global HEALPix cell IDs, one per position along ``cell``.
    level:
        HEALPix level of the IDs.
    attrs:
        Optional attribute mapping to merge (e.g. the source store's
        attributes).

    Returns
    -------
    xarray.Dataset
        Subset with ``cell``, ``latitude``, ``longitude``, and ``crs``
        coordinates and grid-doctor metadata, marked sparse.
    """
    cells = np.asarray(cells, dtype=np.int64)
    if ds.sizes.get("cell") != cells.size:
        raise ValueError(f"Dataset has {ds.sizes.get('cell')} cells but {cells.size} IDs were provided.")
    grid = HealpixGrid(level=level, ellipsoid=_dataset_ellipsoid(ds))
    module, kwargs = _require_healpix_geo_module(grid)
    lon_deg, lat_deg = module.healpix_to_lonlat(cells, level, **kwargs)

    result = ds.assign_coords(
        {
            CELL_DIM: cells,
            LAT_VAR: (CELL_DIM, np.asarray(lat_deg, dtype=np.float64)),
            LON_VAR: (
                CELL_DIM,
                _canonical_lon(np.asarray(lon_deg, dtype=np.float64)),
            ),
        }
    )
    if attrs:
        merged = dict(attrs)
        merged.update(result.attrs)
        result.attrs = merged
    metadata = HealpixMetadata(
        grid,
        Provenance.from_attrs(result.attrs),
        sparse=True,
    )
    return metadata.apply(result)

items.title: Point binning
items.text:
Map point-sampled data (satellite Level-2 swaths, station records, trajectories) onto HEALPix (grid_doctor.swath). Point data cannot use the ESMF weight path: every granule has its own geometry, so weights could never be reused, and nearest-neighbour remapping would spread a narrow swath over the entire globe. Binning assigns each sample to the HEALPix cell that contains it and reduces the samples per cell instead.

See the point data recipe for an end-to-end workflow and the technical decisions for the design rationale.

Bin point-sampled data into HEALPix cells.

Every sample is assigned to the HEALPix cell containing its coordinates (on ellipsoid, consistent with all other grid-doctor output) and all samples per cell are reduced with the requested aggregation.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default ds Dataset

Dataset with per-sample latitude/longitude variables (swath geolocation, station coordinates, …). Variables that span the sample dimensions are binned; variables that share none of the sample dimensions are passed through unchanged; variables that overlap them only partially are skipped with a warning. Non-sample dimensions (time, channel, …) are preserved as batch dimensions.

required level int

Target HEALPix level. Choose it so the cell spacing (58.6° / 2**level) is coarser than the sample spacing: only then is the per-cell mean a faithful stand-in for conservative remapping.

required agg BinAgg | Mapping[str, BinAgg]

Aggregation per variable: a single method applied to all variables or a mapping {variable: method}. Supported methods: "mean" (continuous fields; binning analogue of conservative remapping), "mode" (categorical fields; analogue of nearest-neighbour), "min", "max", and "count". A per-sample sum is deliberately not offered: it scales with sample density (orbit overlap, across-track pixel count) rather than any physical integral.

'mean' nest bool

Use nested HEALPix ordering when True. Nested ordering is required for pyramid coarsening.

True lat_name str | None

Explicit coordinate variable names. When omitted, the standard grid-doctor name lists are searched (latitude, lat, …).

None lon_name str | None

Explicit coordinate variable names. When omitted, the standard grid-doctor name lists are searched (latitude, lat, …).

None source_units SourceUnits

Angular unit convention of the coordinates.

'auto' fill_values Mapping[str, float] | None

Explicit per-variable fill values, e.g. {"cloud_type": 255}. When omitted, declared _FillValue / missing_value attributes are honoured; floating-point non-finite values are always treated as invalid. 0 is accepted as a fill value.

None min_count int

Minimum number of valid samples required for a cell to be valid. Cells with fewer samples are set to NaN (does not apply to "count").

1 with_counts bool

Add an <name>_count companion variable per binned variable holding the number of valid samples per cell. Recommended for published datasets: it makes coverage auditable and enables unbiased merging of overlapping granules downstream.

False dense bool

When True (default), return the full 12 * 4**level cell array with standard grid-doctor coordinates, CRS variable, and attributes, directly consumable by coarsen_healpix and save_pyramid. When False, return a compact dataset containing only the touched cells (the cell coordinate holds the actual HEALPix indices), useful as a per-granule intermediate at high levels; convert with sparse_to_dense before coarsening or publishing.

Ellipsoid of the HEALPix geometry, "sphere" or "WGS84". Defaults to grid_doctor.config.ellipsoid.

def bin_to_healpix(
    ds: xr.Dataset,
    level: int,
    *,
    agg: BinAgg | Mapping[str, BinAgg] = "mean",
    nest: bool = True,
    lat_name: str | None = None,
    lon_name: str | None = None,
    source_units: SourceUnits = "auto",
    fill_values: Mapping[str, float] | None = None,
    min_count: int = 1,
    with_counts: bool = False,
    dense: bool = True,
    ellipsoid: Ellipsoid | None = None,
) -> xr.Dataset:
    """Bin point-sampled data into HEALPix cells.

    Every sample is assigned to the HEALPix cell containing its
    coordinates (on *ellipsoid*, consistent with all other grid-doctor
    output) and all samples per cell are reduced with the
    requested aggregation.

    Parameters
    ----------
    ds:
        Dataset with per-sample latitude/longitude variables (swath
        geolocation, station coordinates, …).  Variables that span the
        sample dimensions are binned; variables that share none of the
        sample dimensions are passed through unchanged; variables that
        overlap them only partially are skipped with a warning.
        Non-sample dimensions (``time``, ``channel``, …) are preserved
        as batch dimensions.
    level:
        Target HEALPix level.  Choose it so the cell spacing
        (``58.6° / 2**level``) is coarser than the sample spacing:
        only then is the per-cell mean a faithful stand-in for
        conservative remapping.
    agg:
        Aggregation per variable: a single method applied to all
        variables or a mapping ``{variable: method}``.  Supported
        methods: ``"mean"`` (continuous fields; binning analogue of
        conservative remapping), ``"mode"`` (categorical fields;
        analogue of nearest-neighbour), ``"min"``, ``"max"``, and
        ``"count"``.  A per-sample *sum* is deliberately not offered:
        it scales with sample density (orbit overlap, across-track
        pixel count) rather than any physical integral.
    nest:
        Use nested HEALPix ordering when *True*.  Nested ordering is
        required for pyramid coarsening.
    lat_name, lon_name:
        Explicit coordinate variable names.  When omitted, the standard
        grid-doctor name lists are searched (``latitude``, ``lat``, …).
    source_units:
        Angular unit convention of the coordinates.
    fill_values:
        Explicit per-variable fill values, e.g. ``{"cloud_type": 255}``.
        When omitted, declared ``_FillValue`` / ``missing_value``
        attributes are honoured; floating-point non-finite values are
        always treated as invalid.  ``0`` is accepted as a fill value.
    min_count:
        Minimum number of valid samples required for a cell to be
        valid.  Cells with fewer samples are set to NaN (does not apply
        to ``"count"``).
    with_counts:
        Add an ``<name>_count`` companion variable per binned variable
        holding the number of valid samples per cell.  Recommended for
        published datasets: it makes coverage auditable and enables
        unbiased merging of overlapping granules downstream.
    dense:
        When *True* (default), return the full ``12 * 4**level`` cell
        array with standard grid-doctor coordinates, CRS variable, and
        attributes, directly consumable by
        [`coarsen_healpix`][grid_doctor.coarsen_healpix] and
        [`save_pyramid`][grid_doctor.save_pyramid].  When
        *False*, return a compact dataset containing only the touched
        cells (the ``cell`` coordinate holds the actual HEALPix
        indices), useful as a per-granule intermediate at high levels;
        convert with
        [`sparse_to_dense`][grid_doctor.swath.sparse_to_dense] before
        coarsening or publishing.
    ellipsoid:
        Ellipsoid of the HEALPix geometry, ``"sphere"`` or
        ``"WGS84"``.  Defaults to ``grid_doctor.config.ellipsoid``.

    Returns
    -------
    xarray.Dataset
        Binned dataset on the HEALPix grid.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        On unknown aggregation methods, invalid levels, or when no
        valid sample coordinates exist.

    Examples
    --------
    ```python
    hpx = gd.bin_to_healpix(
        swath,
        level=11,
        agg={"radiance": "mean", "cloud_type": "mode"},
        fill_values={"cloud_type": 255},
        with_counts=True,
    )
    pyramid = {11: hpx}
    for lvl in range(10, -1, -1):
        pyramid[lvl] = gd.coarsen_healpix(hpx, lvl)
    ```
    """
    if not 0 <= level <= MAX_NESTED_LEVEL:
        raise ValueError(f"level must be within [0, {MAX_NESTED_LEVEL}].")
    if min_count < 1:
        raise ValueError("min_count must be at least 1.")

    lat, lon, sample_dims = resolve_point_coords(ds, lat_name=lat_name, lon_name=lon_name, source_units=source_units)
    # Fail-fast: validate every aggregation before any data is loaded.
    methods = resolve_methods(ds, sample_dims, agg)

    valid_coords = np.isfinite(lat) & np.isfinite(lon)
    if not valid_coords.any():
        raise ValueError("No samples with valid (finite) coordinates found.")

    grid = HealpixGrid.from_nest(level, nest=nest, ellipsoid=_ellipsoid_or_config(ellipsoid))
    module, kwargs = _require_healpix_geo_module(grid)
    cell_ids = np.asarray(
        module.lonlat_to_healpix(lon[valid_coords], lat[valid_coords], depth=level, **kwargs),
        dtype=np.int64,
    )

    # Compact indexing: bin into the touched cells only, scatter later.
    unique_cells, group_idx = np.unique(cell_ids, return_inverse=True)
    group_idx = group_idx.astype(np.int64)
    n_cells = int(unique_cells.size)

    binned: dict[str, xr.DataArray] = {}
    counts: dict[str, xr.DataArray] = {}
    for name, da in ds.data_vars.items():
        var_name = str(name)
        overlap = set(sample_dims) & set(map(str, da.dims))
        if not overlap:
            binned[var_name] = da
            continue
        if overlap != set(sample_dims):
            logger.warning(
                "Skipping %r: covers only part of the sample dimensions %s.",
                var_name,
                sample_dims,
            )
            continue

        method = methods[var_name]

        batch_dims = tuple(d for d in map(str, da.dims) if d not in sample_dims)
        arranged = da.transpose(*batch_dims, *sample_dims)
        fill = (fill_values or {}).get(var_name)
        values = masked_float64(arranged, fill_value=fill)
        values = values.reshape(*arranged.shape[: len(batch_dims)], -1)
        values = values[..., valid_coords]

        valid_count = bin_count(group_idx, values, n_cells=n_cells)

        if method == "count":
            result = valid_count
        elif method == "mode":
            result = bin_mode(group_idx, values, n_cells=n_cells)
            result[valid_count < min_count] = np.nan
        else:
            result = bin_simple(group_idx, values, n_cells=n_cells, func=NPG_FUNC[method])
            result[valid_count < min_count] = np.nan

        attrs = {key: value for key, value in da.attrs.items() if key not in FILL_ATTR_NAMES}
        attrs.update(variable_method_attrs(AGG_TO_METHOD[method]))
        binned[var_name] = xr.DataArray(result, dims=(*batch_dims, "cell"), attrs=attrs)
        if with_counts and method != "count":
            counts[f"{var_name}_count"] = xr.DataArray(
                valid_count.astype(np.int32),
                dims=(*batch_dims, "cell"),
                attrs={"long_name": f"number of valid samples binned into {var_name}"},
            )

    binned.update(counts)
    result_ds = xr.Dataset(binned, attrs=ds.attrs.copy())

    # Preserve batch coordinates (time, channel, ...).
    keep_coords = {
        str(coord): ds.coords[coord]
        for coord in ds.coords
        if not set(sample_dims) & set(map(str, ds.coords[coord].dims))
    }
    result_ds = result_ds.assign_coords(keep_coords)
    method = _dominant_method(result_ds)

    if dense:
        return _scatter_to_dense(result_ds, unique_cells, grid, method=method)
    return _attach_sparse_coords(result_ds, unique_cells, grid, method=method)

def sparse_to_dense(ds: xr.Dataset) -> xr.Dataset:
    """Scatter a compact (sparse) binned dataset onto the full grid.

    Parameters
    ----------
    ds:
        Output of ``bin_to_healpix(..., dense=False)``.

    Returns
    -------
    xarray.Dataset
        Dense dataset with the standard grid-doctor HEALPix coordinates
        and metadata, ready for
        [`coarsen_healpix`][grid_doctor.coarsen_healpix].

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        When *ds* does not look like a sparse binned dataset.
    """
    if not has_healpix_metadata(ds):
        raise ValueError("Dataset doesn't contain healpix metadata.")
    metadata = HealpixMetadata.from_dataset(ds)
    if not metadata.sparse:
        raise ValueError("Dataset is not a sparse binned dataset.")
    cell_ids = np.asarray(ds[CELL_DIM].values, dtype=np.int64)
    return _scatter_to_dense(
        ds.drop_vars([CELL_DIM, LAT_VAR, LON_VAR], errors="ignore"),
        cell_ids,
        metadata.grid,
        method=metadata.provenance.method or "binned-mean",
    )

items.title: Types
items.text:
Shared type aliases used in grid-doctor's signatures. Use them to annotate your own code, e.g. an encoding you build up before passing it to save_pyramid:

from grid_doctor.types import PyramidEncoding

encoding: PyramidEncoding = {
    level: {"ta": {"dtype": "int16", "scale_factor": 0.01}}
    for level in pyramid
}

Special type definitions.

Shared aliases, so that signatures say what a value is instead of Any. The only Any left in grid-doctor's own annotations is the precision parameter of NumPy's generic float type (FloatingArray) and keyword arguments passed through unchanged to third-party functions.

items.title: Weights store
items.text: Remapping weights depend only on the source grid, the HEALPix target and the method, so grid-doctor computes them once and reuses them. Every weight file has one name, derived from what it describes, and lives in a weights store: a local (POSIX) directory. Callers only choose the store's root; everything below it is grid-doctor's layout.

items.title: Getting weights
items.text:
cached_weights is the usual entry point. It returns a local weight file, looking it up in this order:

  1. the store,
  2. the local cache (weights computed while the store was read-only),
  3. otherwise the weights are computed into the store, or into the local cache when the store is read-only.
import grid_doctor as gd

weights_file = gd.cached_weights(ds, level=9)                    # default store
weights_file = gd.cached_weights(ds, level=9, store="/work/ab1234/weights")
pyramid = gd.create_healpix_pyramid(ds, max_level=9, weights_path=weights_file)

regrid_to_healpix and create_healpix_pyramid use the default store when no weights_path is given, so this is enough to compute the weights once and reuse them afterwards:

hp_ds = gd.regrid_to_healpix(ds)  # level derived from the grid resolution

The default store is the GRID_DOCTOR_WEIGHTS_STORE environment variable, or $XDG_CACHE_HOME/grid-doctor/weights (~/.cache/grid-doctor/weights) when it is unset. To compute into an explicit file instead, use compute_healpix_weights(weights_path=...).

Only these choices select a weight file: the source grid, the HEALPix level and the method. Options such as ignore_unmapped, large_file, nproc or prefer_offline change how weights are computed, not the weights themselves. With ignore_unmapped=False, a file found in the store is still checked: it fails if it leaves HEALPix cells unmapped.

items.title: Nested and ring order
items.text:
Weight files are nested; their order is recorded in the grid_doctor_order attribute. Ring and nested weights differ only in how the HEALPix cells are numbered, so ring order is chosen when the weights are applied, and one file serves both:

ds_ring = gd.apply_weight_file(ds, weights_file, nest=False)
pyramid = gd.create_healpix_pyramid(ds, max_level=9, weights_path=weights_file, nest=False)

The target rows are then renumbered in memory (see nested_to_ring); no ESMF run and no second file are needed.

items.title: Sharing weights
items.text:
Point several users or jobs at the same directory to share weights, e.g. GRID_DOCTOR_WEIGHTS_STORE=/work/ab1234/weights. Files are written atomically, so readers never see a partial file. A directory you cannot write to is used read-only: missing weights are computed into your local cache instead.

Only local directories and in-memory filesystems (memory://, for tests) are supported for now.

grid-doctor does not manage permissions: directories and weight files are created as the user's umask, or the directory's default ACL, allows. A store shared between users needs a default ACL on its root, set once by whoever administers it, e.g. for the group ab1234:

setfacl -m g:ab1234:rwx -d -m g:ab1234:rwx /work/ab1234/weights

Every directory and file created below the root then inherits it, whatever each user's umask. A PermissionError on a shared store therefore points at the store's setup, not at grid-doctor.

The same grid is recognised whatever its conventions: coordinates in radians or degrees, longitudes in 0..360 or [-180, 180) and differing variable names all lead to the same weight file.

items.title: Layout
items.text:
Weight files are stored under Hive-style directories, followed by the digest of the source grid:

<root>/version=1/grid=healpix/ellipsoid=sphere/level=9/method=conservative/<digest>.nc
<root>/version=1/grid=healpix/ellipsoid=wgs84/level=9/method=conservative/<digest>.nc

Tools such as pyarrow, DuckDB or Polars read the directory names as columns. One grid has the same digest at every level and method, so WeightsStore.find lists all targets of a grid, or all grids of a target:

from grid_doctor.weights import WeightsStore

store = WeightsStore("/work/ab1234/weights")
store.find(level=9, method="conservative")

Each file also records its identity (source digest, level, indexing scheme, ellipsoid, method, grid-doctor and layout version), the ESMF version and the number of unmapped HEALPix cells as global attributes, so a store can be checked from the files alone.

items.title: Source digest
items.text:
The file name is the SHA-256 digest of the source grid's geometry. It depends only on the cells and their order, so other tools can compute the same digest and share weight files with grid-doctor:

  1. Coordinates. Take the cell-centre latitude and longitude and, if present, the cell-vertex latitude and longitude, in degrees.
  2. Quantise. Round every value to integer micro-degrees, round(value * 1_000_000) (round half to even). Wrap longitudes into [-180_000_000, 180_000_000), so 180 and -180 are equal. Missing vertices (NaN) become -2**63.
  3. Dimensions. Number the dimensions by first appearance, in the order of step 4. A regular grid has lat on (0,) and lon on (1,). An unstructured grid has both on (0,), and its vertices on (0, 1).
  4. Hash. For centre latitude, centre longitude, vertex latitude and vertex longitude in that order, add dims=<dims>;shape=<shape>; (Python tuple notation, e.g. dims=(0, 1);shape=(2, 2);), followed by the integers as little-endian 64-bit values in C (row-major) order.

Variable names, dtypes, units (radians are converted first) and the longitude convention do not change the digest. Cell order does, because it defines the columns of the weight matrix. Vertex coordinates are hashed instead of a node/connectivity list (face_nodes): they describe the same cells and need no shared node numbering between tools.

Source code in grid_doctor/weights.py 
def cached_weights(
    ds: xr.Dataset,
    level: int | None = None,
    *,
    method: RemapMethod = "conservative",
    source_units: SourceUnits = "auto",
    store: WeightsStore | str | Path | None = None,
    ellipsoid: Ellipsoid | None = None,
    **kwargs: Unpack[WeightOptions],
) -> Path:
    """Return a local HEALPix weight file, reusing it through a store.

    Weights are identified by their
    [`WeightsDescription`][grid_doctor.weights.WeightsDescription]: the
    normalised source geometry, the HEALPix target and the method. The
    lookup is done by
    [`WeightsStore.fetch_or_compute`][grid_doctor.weights.WeightsStore.fetch_or_compute].

    Parameters
    ----------
    ds:
        Source dataset whose grid geometry defines the weights.
    level:
        HEALPix level. Derived from the grid resolution when omitted.
    method:
        Weight-generation method. Supported values are `"nearest"` and
        `"conservative"`.
    source_units:
        Unit convention of the source coordinates.
    store:
        Weights store, or its location (see
        [`WeightsStore`][grid_doctor.weights.WeightsStore]). Defaults to
        [`grid_doctor.config.weights_store`][grid_doctor.config.weights_store],
        else the local weights directory.
    ellipsoid:
        Ellipsoid of the HEALPix target, ``"sphere"`` or ``"WGS84"``.
        Defaults to ``grid_doctor.config.ellipsoid``.  Part of
        the weights' identity, so weights are never reused across ellipsoids.
    **kwargs:
        Any additional keyword arguments for
        [`compute_healpix_weights`][grid_doctor.remap.compute_healpix_weights]

    Returns
    -------
    pathlib.Path
        Path to the local NetCDF weight file.

    Examples
    --------
    ```python
    weight_file = cached_weights(ds, level=8, store="/work/ab1234/weights")
    ```
    """
    from .remap import compute_healpix_weights  # remap builds on this module

    ellipsoid = _ellipsoid_or_config(ellipsoid)
    if not isinstance(store, WeightsStore):
        store = WeightsStore(store)
    if level is None:
        level = resolution_to_healpix_level(get_latlon_resolution(ds))

    describe_kwargs = {k: kwargs[k] for k in ("grid", "source_kind", "spectral_transform_command") if k in kwargs}
    source = describe_source(ds, source_units=source_units, **describe_kwargs)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    target = HealpixGrid(level=level, ellipsoid=ellipsoid)  # stored weights are nested
    desc = WeightsDescription(source, target, method)

    def compute(path: Path) -> Path:  # the store holds nested weights; ring is derived from them
        return compute_healpix_weights(
            ds,
            level,
            method=method,
            nest=True,
            source_units=source_units,
            weights_path=path,
            source_description=source,
            ellipsoid=ellipsoid,
            **kwargs,
        )

    path = store.fetch_or_compute(desc, compute)
    if kwargs.get("ignore_unmapped") is False:
        check_coverage(path)  # the stored weights may have been computed ignoring unmapped cells
    return path

items.title: WeightsStore(location=None, *, cache_dir=None, read_only=None)
items.text:
Store of HEALPix weight files, laid out by WeightsRef.

Callers pass a root; everything below it is grid-doctor's layout. The root is a local (POSIX) directory, or an in-memory fsspec filesystem (memory://, mainly for tests). ESMF and the weight readers need local files, so files of in-memory stores are copied once into a local cache that mirrors the same layout.

Args: location: Root of the store: a local path, a file:// or memory:// URL, or an fsspec mapper of either. Defaults to grid_doctor.config.weights_store (environment variable GRID_DOCTOR_WEIGHTS_STORE), else $XDG_CACHE_HOME/grid-doctor/weights. cache_dir: Local directory for copies of in-memory weights and for weights computed while the store is read-only. Defaults to $XDG_CACHE_HOME/grid-doctor/weights. read_only: Forbid publish. When omitted, local stores are read-only if their directory is not writable.

Raises: ValueError: For filesystems other than local and in-memory ones.

Examples: 

store = WeightsStore("/work/ab1234/weights")
if store.exists(desc):
    path = store.fetch(desc)

Source code in grid_doctor/weights.py 
def __init__(  # noqa: D107
    self,
    location: str | Path | FSMap | None = None,
    *,
    cache_dir: str | Path | None = None,
    read_only: bool | None = None,
) -> None:
    from fsspec.core import url_to_fs
    from fsspec.mapping import FSMap

    if location is None:
        location = config.weights_store or local_weights_dir()
    fs: AbstractFileSystem
    if isinstance(location, FSMap):
        fs, root = location.fs, location.root
    elif isinstance(location, (str, os.PathLike)):
        fs, root = url_to_fs(str(location))
    else:
        raise TypeError(
            f"Unsupported weights store location {type(location).__name__!r}; "
            "expected a path, an fsspec URL or an fsspec mapper."
        )
    self.fs = fs
    self.root = str(root).rstrip("/")
    protocols = fs.protocol
    protocols = (protocols,) if isinstance(protocols, str) else tuple(protocols)
    if not _SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS.intersection(protocols):
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unsupported weights store filesystem {protocols[0]!r}; "
            f"expected one of {sorted(_SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS)}."
        )
    self.is_local = bool(_LOCAL_PROTOCOLS.intersection(protocols))
    self._protocol = protocols[0]
    if read_only is None:
        read_only = self.is_local and not _is_writable(Path(self.root))
    self.read_only = read_only
    self.cache_dir = Path(cache_dir) if cache_dir is not None else local_weights_dir()

def local_path(self, item: WeightsDescription | WeightsRef | str) -> Path:
    """Return where the local copy of a weight file lives.

    The file itself for local stores, its place in the local cache

items.title: fetch(item)
items.text:
Return a local path to the weight file, downloading it if needed.

Raises: FileNotFoundError: If the store does not hold the file.

Source code in grid_doctor/weights.py 
def fetch(self, item: WeightsDescription | WeightsRef | str) -> Path:
    """Return a local path to the weight file, downloading it if needed.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If the store does not hold the file.
    """
    path = self._path(item)
    if self.is_local:
        if not self.fs.exists(path):
            raise FileNotFoundError(self.url(item))
        return Path(path)
    local = self.local_path(item)
    if local.exists():
        return local
    if not self.fs.exists(path):
        raise FileNotFoundError(self.url(item))
    logger.info("Copying weight file %s", self.url(item))
    _atomic_write(local, lambda tmp: self.fs.get_file(path, tmp))
    return local

items.title: publish(desc, local_file)
items.text:
Store local_file as the weights of desc and return its reference.

Readers never see a partial file: local stores write a temporary file and rename it.

Raises: PermissionError: If the store is read-only.

Source code in grid_doctor/weights.py 
def publish(self, desc: WeightsDescription, local_file: str | Path) -> WeightsRef:
    """Store *local_file* as the weights of *desc* and return its reference.

    Readers never see a partial file: local stores write a temporary
    file and rename it.

    Raises:
        PermissionError: If the store is read-only.
    """
    if self.read_only:
        raise PermissionError(f"{self!r} is read-only")
    ref = desc.ref
    path = self._path(ref)
    logger.info("Publishing weight file %s", self.url(ref))
    if self.is_local:
        _atomic_write(Path(path), lambda tmp: shutil.copyfile(local_file, tmp))
    else:
        self.fs.makedirs(path.rsplit("/", 1)[0], exist_ok=True)
        self.fs.put_file(str(local_file), path)
    return ref

items.title: fetch_or_compute(desc, compute)
items.text:
Return a local copy of the weights of desc, computing them if needed.

Looks for the local copy, then the store; otherwise calls compute(path) and publishes the result to a writable in-memory store. Weights for a read-only store are computed into and kept in cache_dir only.

The store holds nested-order weights, so compute must write those, whatever the indexing scheme of desc.

Source code in grid_doctor/weights.py 
def fetch_or_compute(self, desc: WeightsDescription, compute: Callable[[Path], Path]) -> Path:
    """Return a local copy of the weights of *desc*, computing them if needed.

    Looks for the local copy, then the store; otherwise calls
    ``compute(path)`` and publishes the result to a writable in-memory
    store. Weights for a read-only store are computed into and kept in
    ``cache_dir`` only.

    The store holds nested-order weights, so *compute* must write
    those, whatever the indexing scheme of *desc*.
    """
    local = self.local_path(desc)
    cached = self.cache_dir / desc.ref.path
    for path in dict.fromkeys((local, cached)):
        if path.exists():
            return path
    if self.exists(desc):
        return self.fetch(desc)
    target = local if (self.is_local and not self.read_only) else cached
    logger.info("Computing HEALPix weight file %s", target)
    target = compute(target)
    if not self.is_local and not self.read_only:
        self.publish(desc, target)
    return target

items.text:
List the weight files whose reference fields match filters.

Args: **filters: Field values of WeightsRef, e.g. level, method or key.

Raises: TypeError: For unknown filter names.

Examples: 

store.find(level=10, method="conservative")

Source code in grid_doctor/weights.py 
def find(self, **filters: Any) -> list[WeightsRef]:
    """List the weight files whose reference fields match *filters*.

    Args:
        **filters: Field values of [`WeightsRef`][grid_doctor.weights.WeightsRef],
            e.g. ``level``, ``method`` or ``key``.

    Raises:
        TypeError: For unknown filter names.

    Examples:
        ```python
        store.find(level=10, method="conservative")
        ```
    """
    fields = set(WeightsRef.__dataclass_fields__)
    unknown = set(filters) - fields
    if unknown:
        raise TypeError(f"Unknown filters: {sorted(unknown)}; expected {sorted(fields)}")
    filters = {k: v.lower() if isinstance(v, str) else v for k, v in filters.items()}
    dirs = (f"{name}={filters.get(name, '*')}" for name in WeightsRef.HIERARCHY)
    pattern = "/".join((*dirs, f"{filters.get('key', '*')}.nc"))
    found = []
    for path in sorted(self.fs.glob(f"{self.root}/{pattern}")):
        try:
            found.append(WeightsRef.parse(str(path).removeprefix(self.root)))
        except ValueError:
            continue
    return found

items.title: describe_source(source, *, grid=None, source_kind='auto', source_units='auto', spectral_transform_command=None, workdir=None)
items.text:
Describe a source for HEALPix weight generation.

Normalises the source geometry and classifies the grid. The mesh and the weight-file metadata are built lazily, so describing a source to look its weights up does not mesh it.

Args: source: Source dataset or source path. A path is mainly useful for spectral inputs that need an external transform. grid: Optional grid dataset that supplies geometry when the data file itself only contains values on dimensions such as cell. source_kind: Explicit source representation. Use "auto" to infer it from the available coordinates. source_units: Angular unit convention of the source coordinates, used to normalise the geometry to degrees. spectral_transform_command: External command used when source_kind="spectral". The command may use {input} and {output} placeholders. workdir: Working directory for the spectral transform; a temporary directory when omitted.

Raises: ValueError: When the geometry cannot be normalised (see normalise_dataset). In particular, cell centres with NaN coordinates (masked grids) are rejected.

Source code in grid_doctor/weights.py 
def describe_source(
    source: xr.Dataset | str | Path,
    *,
    grid: xr.Dataset | None = None,
    source_kind: SourceKind = "auto",
    source_units: SourceUnits = "auto",
    spectral_transform_command: list[str] | tuple[str, ...] | None = None,
    workdir: Path | None = None,
) -> SourceDescription:
    """Describe a source for HEALPix weight generation.

    Normalises the source geometry and classifies the grid. The mesh
    and the weight-file metadata are built lazily, so describing a
    source to look its weights up does not mesh it.

    Args:
        source: Source dataset or source path. A path is mainly
            useful for spectral inputs that need an external transform.
        grid: Optional grid dataset that supplies geometry when the
            data file itself only contains values on dimensions such
            as ``cell``.
        source_kind: Explicit source representation. Use ``"auto"``
            to infer it from the available coordinates.
        source_units: Angular unit convention of the source
            coordinates, used to normalise the geometry to degrees.
        spectral_transform_command: External command used when
            ``source_kind="spectral"``. The command may use
            ``{input}`` and ``{output}`` placeholders.
        workdir: Working directory for the spectral transform;
            a temporary directory when omitted.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When the geometry cannot be normalised (see
            ``normalise_dataset``). In particular, cell centres with
            NaN coordinates (masked grids) are rejected.
    """
    dataset = source if isinstance(source, xr.Dataset) else xr.load_dataset(source)
    kind = source_kind
    if kind == "spectral":
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="grid_doctor_source_") as scratch:
            dataset = _materialise_spectral_source(  # loads eagerly, scratch can go
                source,
                transform_command=spectral_transform_command,
                workdir=workdir or Path(scratch),
            )
        kind = "auto"

    # Only the geometry source is normalised: grid if given, else dataset.
    geometry = normalise_dataset(grid if grid is not None else dataset, source_units)
    kind = _classify_source_kind(geometry, explicit_kind=kind)
    return SourceDescription(dataset=dataset, geometry=geometry, kind=kind)

Lowercase throughout. One name=value directory per entry of HIERARCHY, followed by the source digest as file name::

version=1/grid=healpix/ellipsoid=sphere/level=10/method=conservative/<key>.nc

Every part that changes the weights is a directory, so the path is unique per weight file and the fields used for searching can be read from a listing without opening files. version is the version of the path scheme itself. Files hold nested-order weights; ring order is a renumbering of their rows when they are applied, so it needs no file of its own.

Attributes: method: Remapping method. level: HEALPix level. key: Source digest (sha256 hex digest); see SourceDescription.digest. grid: Target grid; always "healpix". ellipsoid: Ellipsoid of the HEALPix cell vertices, lowercased ("sphere" or "wgs84"). version: Version of the path scheme.
